newsitem.title: USA: UUNET offers Internet fax service.
newsitem.headline: UUNET offers Internet fax service.

text.p: UUNET Technologies Inc, the Internet service provider and unit of WorldCom Inc, said Tuesday it will offer businesses a way to fax over the Internet rather than over voice telephone networks.
The new service, called UUFAX, was developed jointly with Open Port Technology and Ascend Communications Inc.
"Until now, no company has made the investment to deploy a worldwide fax infrastructure which takes advantage of Internet technology," said John Sidgmore, UUNET's CEO and WorldCom vice chairman.
"UUNET is making that investment and we intend to be a leader in the business fax marketplace, which we believe is the next killer application for the Internet," he said in a press release.
WorldCom shares were up 1/8 to 31-3/4 in early afternoon trading.

UUFAX allows people to send faxes to and from stand-alone fax machines or desktop computers as well as send e-mail and e-mail attachments as faxes. The service also supports broadcast faxing, the company said.
Users can track their faxes and compile data on fax usage with the service, which runs over UUNET's own Internet backbone.

The company said Bear Stearns Cos Inc, Chevron Corp and SourceFinder have agreed to use UUFAX during its beta test period, scheduled to begin this month. The service will be available commercially later this year.
